Vanessa — thanks for the draft. A few carveouts we need clarified before we can move to internal counsel: 

1) Broad ‘audit rights’ language: we can’t agree to unlimited inspection access. Please propose either (A) artifact delivery + sampled inspection windows or (B) ephemeral staging access with a hardened jumpbox and scoped logging.

2) Pen test language: our security team requires a 30–60 day notice window, sampling bands that limit production impact, and a defined list of allowed tools (no credential dumping or social engineering). Can you confirm Redwood’s typical pen-test approach and whether you’ll accept a mutually-agreed toolset?

3) SOC 2 evidence: we expect the latest SOC 2 Type II + the security design doc and a 1-year history of control exceptions. If anything else is needed (e.g., syslog extracts), let us know the format and retention we can expect.

I’ve attached a redline of the order form for our proposed edits (redlined_orderform_v3.docx). Marcus — looping you for the technical ops constraints.

Hi Sarah — appreciate the clear notes and the redline. High level: we can support both inspection models you outlined; choosing between them mainly changes the operational handoffs and timelines. Below are two pragmatic options we typically offer and the evidence cadence we recommend. Please pick the one that fits Clearpath’s compliance posture and we’ll incorporate the language into the MSA/order form redline.

Option A — Artifact-first + bounded inspection (lower operational friction)
- Deliverables: SOC 2 Type II report, architecture diagram, control narrative, latest pen-test report (redacted) and a 30-day bundle of audit logs (syslog / API traces) for sampled dates.
- Inspection: sample windows (2 x 2 business days per 12 months) where we provide screen-share and ticketed evidence requests. No live admin access to production.
- Pen-test: 45-day notice preferred; sampling bands defined in matrix; mutually-agreed toolset; vulnerability remediation SLA 60 days for P1/P2.
- Evidence cadence: quarterly packets (docs + 30-day log slices) + ad-hoc sampled requests with 5 business day SLAs for fulfillment.

Option B — Ephemeral staging access (higher assurance, more ops lift)
- Deliverables: same baseline artifacts.
- Inspection: ephemeral staging environment provided for inspection sessions (access expires automatically), hardened jumpbox with MFA and session recording; access granted with 14–30 day notice depending on scope.
- Pen-test: 30-day notice acceptable for staging; production tests require 45-day notice and an ops runbook.
- Evidence cadence: monthly artifacts for 3 months post-activation, then quarterly thereafter.

Attachments I’m including for our internal/legal team: pen_test_scope_matrix.xlsx (defines sampling bands/tools) and evidence_rhythm.md (proposed cadence).

Asked of you: which option do you prefer? If neither, we can craft hybrid language (e.g., artifact-first with a one-time ephemeral session per year).

I’ll loop Karthik and Ben for the exact redline language and to confirm remediation SLAs.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Sarah — thanks for the quick turnaround while you were preparing the redline. Clearpath’s preferred path (per our call) was Option B (ephemeral staging access) with a couple of clarifying points; below is a consolidated summary of agreed items that I’ll incorporate into the formal redline and DocuSign packet.

Agreed (summary):
- Inspection model: Ephemeral staging environment (non-prod) for active inspections. Access is timeboxed, granted via a hardened jumpbox, MFA enforced, session-recorded. Production access is explicitly prohibited except for emergency escalations requiring pre-authorized SOP.
- Notice windows: Staging access — 14 business days minimum (for standard inspections); Production-impacting tests — 45 calendar days with a mutually-agreed ops runbook.
- Pen-test constraints: Allowed tools will be scoped in the pen_test_scope_matrix.xlsx we exchanged. No credential harvesting, no social-engineering, and no noisy destructive checks without prior written consent.
- Evidence deliverables: Redwood will deliver SOC 2 Type II report, architecture diagram, control narrative, and a 30-day log bundle in JSONL format for sampled days. Additional artifacts (config dumps, test evidence) available on request with 5 business day SLAs.
- Remediation SLA: We commit to 60 days for P1/P2 items; 90 days for P3. For critical production-blocking issues, we will provide a mitigation plan within 7 business days.
- Sampling cadence: Initial onboarding — weekly artifact packets for first month after go-live; thereafter monthly for 2 months; then quarterly ongoing. One ephemeral staging session will be available per 12 months; additional sessions negotiable.
